title: Choose the visual world for Mother AI
question: The roll assigned Care Signal. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Care Signal
options.lineage: The green / amber / red traffic-light card parents are given for a feverish child under five
options.thesis: The colour in the app means something: green is fine to handle at home, amber means call your GP today, red means get help now.
options.viewport: Home opens on one big line (‘What’s on your mind?’), the ask field right under it, the child it’s about as a tap-to-switch chip, then recent chats each marked with its care colour.
options.risk: Could feel clinical if the three signal colours leak into decoration. They must only ever mean a level of care, and most screens stay green and calm.

raised.raise: Say it once: a care level is one coloured band, never a badge plus a label plus an icon.
One large headline per screen on a strict 4-pt grid. Everything else stays small and neutral.
Each conversation runs down one vertical rail, and every answer marks its care level on it.
Guidance is set as numbered steps in a strict margin column, not as a paragraph.
Every quantity (ages, temperatures, read times) uses tabular figures so numbers line up.
Pushed screens slide in as weighted sheets over the page and settle slightly, rather than hard-cutting.

options.label: The Red Book
options.lineage: The parent-held child health record: the UK Red Book and the German Mutterpass
options.thesis: Each child is a booklet with a coloured cover, and every chat is written into it as an entry.
options.viewport: Home is a stack of your children’s booklets. Open one to ask about that child, with past entries below.
options.risk: The most familiar idea for this category. It also drifts toward a journal or tracker, which the MVP deliberately avoids.

options.label: Factory catalog sleeve
options.lineage: Peter Saville’s numbered Factory Records sleeves
options.thesis: Everything is a catalog number decoded by colour.
options.viewport: A black field with one pulse plot and a numbered index.
options.risk: A dark, coded world. It breaks the light theme you asked for.
options.case: Fuses poorly: an anxious parent needs plain words, not a code to decode.
options.kept: Say it once: nothing is labelled twice.

options.label: Crouwel grid specimen
options.thesis: Letterforms built cell by cell on a visible grid.
options.viewport: Huge grid-built headline over a visible construction grid.
options.risk: Reads as a type poster, not a companion.
options.case: Fuses poorly: parents don’t recognise it, and a visible grid adds noise to a chat.
options.kept: The grid’s discipline and one monumental headline per screen.

options.label: Mesophotic deep dive
options.thesis: One vertical depth axis rules every line.
options.viewport: A descending depth profile with readouts.
options.risk: Dark and cold: the wrong emotional temperature.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a conversation is not a descent.
options.kept: One vertical rail ruling each conversation.

options.label: Orizuru fold sequence
options.thesis: One sheet folded in numbered steps.
options.viewport: A red square with numbered fold steps down the margin.
options.risk: Beautiful but foreign to the parent’s world.
options.case: Fuses poorly on identification, though it holds clarity for step-by-step guidance.
options.kept: Numbered steps in a strict margin column.

options.label: Oscilloscope bench
options.thesis: Every value is measured against a graticule.
options.viewport: A live trace on a ten-division grid.
options.risk: A dark lab instrument. Too technical and anxious for this audience.
options.kept: Numbers in tabular figures, always aligned.

options.label: Darkroom exposure record
options.lineage: Printer’s exposure cards with tracing overlays
options.thesis: Overlapping translucent sheets that slide aside.
options.viewport: Stacked sheets over a backlit zone ramp.
options.risk: Hatching and zone numbers mean nothing to a parent.
options.kept: Screens move as weighted sheets over the page.

canonCard.label: Soft wellness companion
canonCard.thesis: What parenting apps usually ship: pastel lavender, rounded cards, friendly illustration.
canonCard.viewport: Greeting, pastel prompt card, child cards, article card.
canonCard.risk: Close to what the app is today, and hard to tell apart from competitors.
